verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component of this is either published in the admissible corpus or already the level. The note itself is stored (docs/d8fad12136d81c02b77cfcbd69e21b0145c1d1ec.txt) and indexed in snapshots/20260902T152400Z.json, which clean-view lists as admissible - so its thesis was publicly readable six weeks before the print. The facts it interprets are the most heavily reported events in this name's year: the 2026-06-04 beat-and-raise and the 13.7% sell-off are in the baseline history as -13.66%, and the 43.5% de-rating from the 06-02 peak is the baseline's own pct_from_52w_high of -43.52%. That leaves only the interpretation - 'the results were not the problem, the expectation stack was' - and an interpretation of a completed 43% de-rating is not a new fact about the coming quarter; it is a restatement of the price. This is also the argument I am specifically instructed not to accept in reverse, so I will not accept it forward either: 'the stock has fallen a long way, therefore the setup is asymmetric' is the run-up doing duty for a distribution, and it is undated. The supporting option argument is now checkable and it cuts against the finding rather than for it. A real, pre-print implied move exists in the admissible sweep: 'Ciena options suggest 9.4% stock move after earnings release' appears as a title in search_trace/20260902T152400Z.json, and a Benzinga 'Broadcom Week: 10 Stocks Set For Double-Digit Moves' piece is indexed in the same admissible snapshot. A 9.4% implied move on a 12.9% historical median is not the market ignoring positioning risk; it is the market pricing a large move and pricing it slightly below a median that is itself dominated by two outliers. Contamination note, since I am the independent check here: every document this finding cites is in a clean-view-admissible snapshot and is dated before the print, and the chain from the 07-19 note plus the -43.5% de-rating to a bullish tilt is fully reconstructible without knowing the outcome - so I find no sign of answer-aiming in its construction, only in its confidence.

So an article whose thesis is 'the insane opportunity for companies like Marvell and Ciena' was in the public news stream three weeks before the print - that is not an unaggregated divergence, that is the aggregation. Lumentum's 15%, Coherent's 9% and Corning's 5% were each their own headline event on their own day, and the fact that Ciena fell while they rose is the price bars, which is where I am told to look first: the market saw the supplier results and sold Ciena anyway, which is the market's answer to the read-through, not its absence. The mechanism is also genuinely two-sided in a way the finding half-concedes: Lumentum and Coherent are Ciena's upstream vendors, so record component demand and record component pricing are as easily a gross-margin headwind for the systems buyer as a volume tailwind, and the corpus contains an item taking the opposite view of the same complex ('Optics Stocks Divide'). Its own independence field says the range crosses zero, which is the correct read and is close to saying there is no edge here.

The residual is timing rather than fact, and the timing argument does not survive contact with the mechanics: the densest Form 4 day coinciding with a 9% down session is what 10b5-1 plan sales look like when they are pooled on a scheduled window, and the 09-02 Form 4 is a single filing with no size in the capture. Against a $56.6bn market cap and 2.0m shares a day of turnover, executive sales would have to be extraordinary to matter, and no share count or dollar value for any Form 4 or 144 is stored, so the magnitude is not merely small - it is absent. Note too that a Form 4 reports a transaction that has already happened, so the supply it describes is behind the tape rather than in front of it.
